stage1.impression: A believable dusk street elevation: the tree, the weathered render on the neighbours and the warm room seen through the glass come close to a photograph, and the interior with its record wall, bar and globe lamp is the best part. But the shopfront is the darkest thing in the frame. The flats' white bay boxes and the pale pavement outshine it, the frosted pane at left reads as a dead dark panel with a ghost on it rather than a glowing lightbox, there is no blue-hour sky tone, the EARF letters read as flat beige vinyl, and the speaker is a grey sliver at the window's edge. At this stage a magazine would see a generic, nicely lit shopfront rather than a specific place.

blocking_9: The frosted lightbox must glow evenly as the shopfront's brightest plane, with the dancing silhouette legible: region [300,370,420,610] lum_median 70-110 and its y-falloff within about 15%
The shopfront and lit room must be the brightest mass in the frame, brighter than the flats above and the pavement: the window [440,360,740,620] lum_median above the facade [260,0,760,200]
A real blue-hour balance: cool facades and street against the 2400-2700 K interior (the facades' b_median at or above r_median), not the current grey-beige
An EARF speaker must read at a glance through the glass, not as a 27 px grey sliver at the frame of the pane
The pavement's light pools need a believable source and must not be brighter than the shop; the hot cream threshold in the doorway must come down
The etched name must read as etched/frosted glass (soft, slightly luminous, with a polished edge), not opaque beige vinyl

defects.what: Frosted lightbox not lit: median 20, flatter than the room beside it; the dancing woman reads as a ghostly reflection, not a fogged silhouette behind frosting
Flats' white bay boxes and blinds are the brightest area in the frame (median 104), clean CG-white with no grime, and they pull the eye off the shop
Pavement is brighter (median 70) than the shopfront and reads as a smooth CG slab; light pools at 480-560 and 680-760 x 740-800 come from no visible lamp
Doorway threshold floor is a hot flat cream patch (median 164) that reads as a lit plinth rather than a floor
EARF letters opaque, flat salmon-beige (median 155) with no glass behaviour or edge glow; read as a sticker
The only speaker visible is a sliver in a niche at the pane's right edge, grey and partly behind the mullion; no hero, no colour
Blackened-steel stall riser and frames crushed toward black (median 23) with no sheen or edge highlight from the street lamps
Neighbour's upper window a flat black void (crush 15% in region); lower blind panel flat and evenly lit
No sky or ambient blue anywhere; white balance 3400 K neutralises blue hour into dusk grey
Entry vestibule's stone cladding blotchy and tiled-looking at 1:1

changes.problem: The frosted lightbox, a subject named on the card, is unlit and reads as a dark, dead pane with a ghost in it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 20.4, p95 30.9; y-profile 10-24, darker than the room glass beside it (median 21-32)

change.setting: the lightbox's emission (not in the card's settings; add it as a glowing surface behind the frosted pane, warm white about 2700 K)
change.to: emission about 1.5-2.5, evenly back-lit, with the silhouette printed on an inner layer 30-50 mm behind the frosting so it fogs

changes.expected: The left pane becomes an even warm-white glow with a soft, legible dancing figure. It reads as the shop's sign and makes the place specific.

changes.problem: There is no blue hour: the grade neutralises the ambient light, so the facades and pavement are grey-beige and the warm room has nothing cool to contrast with.

evidence.measured: r 99 / g 81 / b 68 on the neighbouring render; the pavement is r 76 / b 67

change.to: 4300 (keep tint -6), with the street's sky/world colour shifted to deep blue about #2A3A5C

changes.expected: The facades and street go cool blue-grey and the interior stays amber, giving the classic dusk split.

changes.problem: The flats above and the pavement outshine the shopfront, so the eye lands on the white bay boxes.

change.to: 150 W, 3000 K, placed so one is visible or implied at frame left and none lights the upper storey; add a 30% darker grime/age map to the bay boxes' white paint

changes.expected: The upper storey drops to a supporting mid-tone and the shop becomes the brightest mass.

changes.problem: The room behind the glass is underexposed relative to the street, so the record wall, the bar and the speaker barely carry.

change.setting: the record wall 4 x spot / the Domes' downlights

changes.expected: The interior reads as the warm heart of the frame: shelves, bar top and the niche readable from across the street.

changes.problem: The only visible speaker is a grey sliver at the right edge of the pane, half hidden by the frame, so the product is not the hero.

evidence.measured: 27 px wide, r 79 / g 59 / b 41, lum_median 62

change.to: about [-11.0, -0.6, 1.5] at [0.0, 3.6, 1.9], so the sightline through the centre pane lands on a back-bar niche speaker or the altar pair rather than the door pier

changes.expected: One Atmosphere speaker sits clear in a pane, its silhouette and back-lit acrylic legible at a glance.

changes.problem: The etched name reads as opaque beige vinyl, not etched glass.

evidence.measured: lum_median 155, r 187 / g 148 / b 125, fully opaque, hard 18 px edge with no inner glow

change.setting: the window's etched name emission, plus its material
change.to: 0.04, frosted translucent (transmission ~0.6, roughness 0.5) so the room shows through softly

changes.expected: The letters read as satin-frosted glass picking up the interior's glow, about 90-120 in luminance, not a flat sticker.

changes.problem: The pavement is a smooth, overbright CG slab whose hot pools come from no visible lamp, and the doorway threshold is a flat hot patch.

change.setting: the floor's polish / pavement material and the vestibule light
change.to: darker, damp, broom-finished concrete (albedo -35%, roughness map 0.35-0.7 with joints and staining); threshold material a darker stone, or its spill reduced 50%

changes.expected: The street sits dark, with soft reflections of the shop's glow, and the threshold reads as a lit floor rather than a light box.

changes.problem: The blackened-steel stall riser and frames are crushed with no sheen, so the shopfront's key material does not read.

change.to: blackened steel with roughness 0.35-0.5 variation, brown patina, and a crisp edge highlight catching the street lamp

changes.expected: The riser reads as metal, with an uneven soft sheen and bright arrises.

out_of_scope.request: A tinted (coloured) speaker so the frame has one saturated note
out_of_scope.why: Configuration is Smoke and the products' colour is fixed; the frame has no saturated colour as a result, which the brief accepts for this configuration

out_of_scope.request: Relocate a speaker or the lightbox closer to the glass
out_of_scope.why: The room's layout and the shopfront are fixed by the card
